label: Post
summary: A longer personal post built from one story: an opening scene, what develops from it, and what it means now.

slots.label: Hook Scene
slots.description: The specific moment, image, or honest claim the post opens on — concrete enough to picture, not a topic statement.

slots.label: Development
slots.description: The memory or relationship thread that builds from the opening scene — the tension, turn, or complication the post moves through.

slots.label: Takeaway
slots.description: What the moment means now — the earned reflection the post lands on, not a generic or unearned lesson.

research.basis: 'One story, one point' at essay length maps onto the classic scene-complication-reflection arc and Gornick's situation-vs-story split; concreteness and narrative transportation both argue for opening on a scene rather than a thesis.
citations: Graham (paulgraham.com/essay.html) — surprise without generality is gossip, generality without surprise is a textbook; an essay lands on one idea
Gornick, The Situation and the Story — situation (what happened) vs story (what the author has come to say) as two layers a piece must combine
Sadoski, Goetz & Rodriguez 2000 — concreteness effect: abstract openings measurably lose readers before the story starts
Green & Brock 2000 — narrative transportation: sustained space allows real absorption, though the effect remains modest
